name: Chuck Grassley
role: U.S. Senator from Iowa (since 1981; House 1975-1981); President pro tempore of the Senate; long-time Judiciary and Finance committee chair
summary: Grassley is a Republican senator known for fiscal conservatism, support for tax cuts and a balanced-budget amendment, opposition to the Affordable Care Act and to expanded gun control, and socially conservative positions on abortion and marriage. He also leads whistleblower, FOIA, farm-payment-limit and biofuel efforts, backs NATO and Ukraine aid, supports USMCA while criticising tariffs, and stresses Congress's Article I role against executive overreach.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted against the 2009 Affordable Care Act, warning it slid toward government control of health care, and as Finance chairman called government-run health care "a slogan, not an answer" in response to the CBO Medicare for All report.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted against the $10.10 minimum wage bill in 2014 and the $15 Sanders amendment in 2021 (he had supported a 2007 increase paired with small-business tax relief). The recent record is consistent opposition to a substantial raise; votes only, so medium.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argues against government-run health care and against government dictating drug prices (his own drug-pricing bill keeps government out of price-setting), but also champions ethanol mandates and farm programmes, so the evidence is mixed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2012 floor statement opposed President Obama's proposal to raise taxes on households above $250,000, arguing the wealthy already pay the bulk of federal taxes and higher rates do not raise revenue; he later voted for the 2017 tax law.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Leads bills to restrain the largest digital platforms (American Innovation and Choice Online Act), yet opposes government price-setting for drugs and other Democratic regulatory proposals; the evidence points both ways.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In 2025 floor remarks he supported Medicaid work requirements for able-bodied adults, saying the way out of poverty is work and that work requirements apply to every other government programme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Cosponsors the Death Tax Repeal Act, calling the estate tax "purely punitive", and in 2025 voted for a reconciliation law that raised the exemption.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His 2019 WSJ op-ed called steel and aluminum tariffs a tax on Americans that should go, and in 2025 he co-led the Trade Review Act to require congressional approval; but he voted in April and October 2025 against resolutions ending the tariff emergency. Words and record pull apart, so low.

free-trade.rationale: Voted for the Panama and Colombia trade agreements in 2011, led USMCA through the Finance Committee, wrote that he has been involved in the passage of every U.S. free-trade agreement, and says Iowa depends on fair and free trade. He criticises tariffs rather than asserting the statement itself.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Cosponsors a constitutional Balanced Budget Amendment to force Congress to live within its means (2017 Q&A) and voted for the 2011 balanced budget amendment.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted against the 2009 Recovery Act and the 2021 American Rescue Plan, and presents deficit discipline and the balanced budget amendment as against "Big Spenders".

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted for the 2008 bank rescue (TARP) but opposed the 2008 auto bailout, saying taxpayers should not rescue companies whose own investors will not help; mixed.

farm-price-support.rationale: Backs preserving crop insurance and temporary assistance for sudden price drops and voted for the 2018 farm bill, but wants hard payment limits and rejects open-ended subsidies.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted in 2009 and 2010 to protect and reauthorize the DC Opportunity Scholarship Program, a federal voucher programme for DC children; votes only, and the programme is limited to low-income DC students.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Voted in 2023 for the joint resolution overturning the Biden administration's student-loan waiver rule, and elsewhere calls the plan a bailout.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Cosponsored the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act (S. 2342, 2021); cosponsorship alone is medium.

ban-cartels.rationale: Sponsors the American Innovation and Choice Online Act, which would let enforcers challenge dominant platforms that abuse market power to stifle competition; it restrains rather than breaks up concentrated power.

public-service-media.rationale: Voted against an amendment to strike the 2025 rescission of Corporation for Public Broadcasting funding, i.e. for defunding it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Voted against the 2013 Whitehouse amendment on a carbon pollution fee; only one vote on a narrow case, so low.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted against the Green New Deal resolution (2019) and the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act, and in 2023 remarks accepted that climate changes but dismissed "unsubstantiated assertions of impending disaster" and called for practical approaches.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said in 2023 that oil and gas are critical to lowering energy costs and called the Biden administration's approach a "war on fossil fuels"; voted for a 2021 amendment to cancel the Biden ban on federal oil and gas leasing. He also champions biofuels, so he is not single-minded.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Argued on the floor in 2018 for reauthorizing FISA Section 702 because those who protect the country must have the tools to keep it safe, citing terrorist attacks, and voted for the 2024 reauthorization.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question (marijuana only), not this statement.

limit-guns.rationale: Calls the right to bear arms an individual, fundamental right and rejects stricter gun control as unwise and unconstitutional (2016 floor statement); voted for his own records-focused amendment in 2013 instead of expanded checks, against the assault weapons ban amendment, and against the 2022 Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.

empower-police-military.rationale: Says he has always backed the blue and is not for defunding the police, and backed law-enforcement funding in the 2025 reconciliation bill; he did not speak to expanding police authority.

decide-locally.rationale: His Electoral College Q&A says limiting centralized government puts decisions in the hands of local citizen-neighbors and that election laws are reserved to the states; stated mainly for elections, so low.

rehabilitation.rationale: On the First Step Act he said prisons must do more than punish and deter, and backed recidivism-reduction programmes and earned credits, while insisting sentences stay tough enough to deter; both aims are stated.

death-penalty.rationale: Offered the 2011 Judiciary Committee amendment making terrorists who use weapons of mass destruction eligible for the death penalty, saying the most serious crimes should carry the most serious penalties.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Said in 2018 that he supports mandatory minimum sentences to help law enforcement take down criminal enterprises, while the First Step Act eased them for nonviolent offenders and broadened mandatory penalties for the worst criminals.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Backs the Respect for Rights of Conscience Act exempting religious institutions from the health-law contraception mandate, calling the mandate unconstitutional, and in 2022 cited religious-liberty lawsuits as his reason for opposing the Respect for Marriage Act.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: In a 2020 op-ed he supported a Senate resolution for the global repeal of blasphemy, heresy and apostasy laws as violations of religious freedom.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: His 2020 op-ed calls blasphemy laws a vehicle for egregious violations of religious freedom and backs a Senate resolution urging their global repeal.

traditional-family.rationale: At his 2011 Judiciary hearing statement he defended traditional one-man, one-woman marriage as the foundation of society and said civilizations were built on it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for DOMA (1996) and the marriage amendment (2004) and said in 2011 that he supports marriage between one man and one woman; in 2022 he voted against the Respect for Marriage Act but said his vote was not about opposing recognition of same-sex marriages. Mixed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Welcomed the Dobbs ruling, saying the unborn's right to life must be protected, and in 2025 floor remarks hailed states being re-empowered to protect life in the womb; voted for bans on taxpayer-funded abortion and the born-alive bill.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposed the Equality Act's gender-identity provisions in 2021, and in 2026 chaired a hearing arguing that biological women should not have to accommodate male-born athletes in women's sports.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Voted against the 2010 Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act; a vote alone is medium.

voter-id.rationale: Cosponsors the SAVE America Act and in his 2026 Q&A argues voters should show proof of citizenship to register and a government photo ID to vote.

collective-defense.rationale: In a 2024 NATO anniversary speech he called NATO the most successful military alliance and said the U.S. would respond to defend an ally; voted 100-0 to reaffirm Article 5 (2017) and for Finland and Sweden joining NATO (2022).

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His 2024 NATO speech argues for keeping the alliance and American leadership in it, and he voted to add Finland and Sweden.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Defends NATO against Russia and calls Russia an adversary, supporting aid to Ukraine, rather than neutrality between blocs.

military-superiority.rationale: In his 2024 "Peace Through Strength" series he says the U.S. and its allies must keep militaries strong enough to deter war and prevent aggression.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2010 he said having a home for Jewish people is a very legitimate thing and criticised Palestinians for not recognising Israel's right to exist.

force-without-un.rationale: Voted for the 2002 Iraq force authorization and against the Levin amendment that would have required a new UN Security Council resolution first; votes only.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Voted against the UN disabilities convention, citing infringement of U.S. sovereignty by a UN monitoring committee reviewing U.S. disability law.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposed joining the UN disabilities convention because a UN committee would criticise U.S. laws, which he called an infringement on sovereignty.

multipolar-world.rationale: In 2024 he criticised the Putin-Xi "multipolar world" idea and defended a U.S.-led post-Cold War order.

national-self-determination.rationale: His 2024 speech criticises the idea that big powers may dominate neighbours against their peoples' will and welcomes former captive nations choosing their own course.

separated-powers.rationale: Says the Constitution built checks and balances so no branch, party or region gets too powerful; as Finance chairman and again in 2025 he pushed to reclaim Congress's Article I tariff power from the executive.

second-chamber.rationale: Describes the Senate as designed with longer terms to cool the passions of the moment alongside the directly elected House, and defends that two-house design.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Defends the Electoral College and opposes abolishing it; says changes should come only by constitutional amendment.

public-access-to-information.rationale: His op-ed champions FOIA and a statutory presumption of openness, saying open government is the lifeblood of good government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Opening the 2015 'Going Dark' hearing he called devices encrypted so that even the company cannot unlock them under a warrant 'a dangerous state of affairs' and asked how to give law enforcement judicially sanctioned access; in 2016 he pressed for a solution that lets law enforcement keep that ability. He framed it as an open question and backed no bill, so medium.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His 2016 floor statement calls the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms an individual, fundamental constitutional right on a par with free speech and religion, which rules out restricting arms to the army and police.

notes: Living person: answers rest on his votes (Senate roll-call XML), bill records, floor speeches, op-eds and press-release statements; everything else is null. senate.gov and grassley.senate.gov block automated fetches, so their pages and vote files were read from Internet Archive copies of the same URLs; the URLs cited are the originals. Voteview was used only to find roll-call numbers. Votes alone are medium. Where his own words and recent votes conflict (tariffs; same-sex marriage; TARP vs auto bailout) the answer is mixed at low. The first-pass search summary attributed a "political violence has no place" post to him after the Kirk assassination; the source shows that wording was Sen. Ernst's, so political-violence-never stays null. Whistleblower law itself (False Claims Act amendments, whistleblower protections) matches no statement directly. Searches on immigration levels, unions, term limits, nuclear power and school prayer found no statement of his on the wording, so those stay null. Opus deepening pass (2026-10-31) on line 12: added state-arms-monopoly (from his 2016 Second Amendment floor statement) and unbreakable-encryption (2015 Going Dark hearing statement and 2016 release, read in reprints because grassley.senate.gov refuses fetches). Searched and left null: political-violence-never (his statements condemn specific attacks, the Jan. 6 riot and 'violence in our democracy', not political violence as such; a campaign-account post was not his Senate record), immigrants-learn-language (he voted for the 2006 and 2007 Inhofe 'English as national language' amendments, but their naturalization provisions could not be read in the original), restrict-foreign-funding, open-government-data and arms-reduction (no statement on the wording found).
